hook: François Chollet created Keras, the deep learning library that became a default entry point into neural networks for millions of developers, while working as a Google engineer for close to a decade. In 2019 he published the ARC-AGI benchmark, arguing that measuring intelligence required tasks a system could not memorize its way through, and in 2024 he put a million dollars behind a public prize to beat it. He left Google in November 2024 to co-found Ndea with former Zapier president Mike Knoop, betting that program synthesis rather than further scaling is the more promising path toward general AI systems.

quick_facts: Created Keras in 2015, which Google says reached more than two million developers
Worked at Google for close to a decade before leaving in November 2024
Published the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC-AGI) benchmark and the paper On the Measure of Intelligence in November 2019
Launched the ARC Prize in 2024, a $1 million competition to beat the ARC-AGI benchmark
Co-founded Ndea in 2024 with Mike Knoop, former president of Zapier, to pursue program-synthesis approaches to AGI
Author of Deep Learning with Python, first published in 2017

achievements.title: Created Keras, 2015
achievements.impact: Built the deep learning API that Google says reached more than two million users and underpins systems at Waymo, YouTube, Netflix and Spotify.

achievements.title: Published the ARC-AGI benchmark, 2019
achievements.impact: Introduced a reasoning benchmark designed to resist memorization, reframing how the field measures progress toward general intelligence.

achievements.title: Launched the ARC Prize, 2024
achievements.impact: Put up a $1 million prize for beating the ARC-AGI benchmark, pushing outside researchers to compete on the problem in public.

achievements.impact: Left Google to start a company betting on program synthesis, rather than further model scaling, as a route to more general AI.
